protected_invariants: the R2 provider class is preserved rather than relaxed: `cloudflare-r2` keeps `auto` as its only region, keeps the account-subdomain rule (a suffix test, so a host that merely contains r2.cloudflarestorage.com and ends elsewhere is refused, and the bare registrable domain is refused because it names no account), and the twenty pre-existing identity tests in this file pass unmodified, which is the evidence that the second class widened the enum without moving the first one

there is no arbitrary-host fail-open: the endpoint must belong to the provider that names it, so the self-hosted class cannot be reached by declaring cloudflare-r2 and cannot be pointed at a host outside the operator's own network, and the region is validated per provider rather than against a flat union because a union would admit the two cross pairs (cloudflare-r2 with us-east-1, self-hosted-s3 with auto) that name no real target

the self-hosted class cannot address the current machine or an arbitrary public destination: loopback is refused with its own message, a publicly routable address is refused, a DNS name is refused because resolving one is a network call the loader does not make, and an IPv6 endpoint is refused for every provider class because none of them admits one

the endpoint field must read as the address it dials: the raw spelling in the identity file is compared against the parsed host, because the URL parser rewrites the WHATWG legacy IPv4 forms (192.168.011.070 is read with octal octets as 192.168.9.56 and the short form 192.168.11 as a 24-bit tail as 192.168.0.11) and both rewrites land inside a range a range test alone would admit, so a spelling that denotes a different host than it appears to is refused rather than silently dialled

no part of the create-only path is changed: the requirement remains `If-None-Match: '*'` on `PutObject`, a HEAD-then-PUT emulation is never used, 412 (and 409 where a proxy reports it that way) remains the only benign collision, and the transport contract still admits exactly the five verbs it admitted before with no delete verb added; the repository does not claim that a self-hosted endpoint honours the condition, and the contract records that this must be established for that endpoint by live evidence
the offline CLIs scripts/ops/stage_d_backup_snapshot.js and scripts/ops/stage_d_restore_verify.js are byte-unchanged and remain netless, and neither live CLI is changed by this mission

there is no implicit credential discovery anywhere on the live path: this mission changes the non-secret addressing loader only, and the secret half is byte-unchanged -- no default location, no ~/.aws, no AWS_PROFILE, no AWS_* environment variable, no instance metadata and no SDK provider chain

no credential, API token or secret value is created, requested, read, printed, logged, copied or persisted by this mission, CREDENTIAL_CREATED=NO and CREDENTIAL_VALUE_INSPECTED=NO, no credential value appears in the repository, the diff, a test fixture or an evidence file, and every value in the tests stays synthetic and marked so that a leak would be detectable rather than asserted absent

the target identity remains a closed nine-field schema: no field is added or removed, the schema version stays `stage-d-live-target-identity/v1`, and the new rules are constraints on the values of the existing `provider`, `endpoint` and `region` fields
every test in this mission runs offline under the existing network tripwire, which asserts zero attempts at the end of each file, so the widened class is proven without contacting any endpoint

no production state is mutated and no live request is made: no backup, restore, authority mutation, live fetch, DB write, raw write, training, prediction, backtest, model activation or migration apply is executed, and no object is written to any target
no new runtime dependency is added and package.json and package-lock.json are unchanged
Stage D is not started and no gate is advanced: BLOCKER_3 stays OPEN, GATE_2 stays NOT_ACCEPTED, GATE_3 stays NOT_AUTHORIZED and STAGE_D_STARTED=NO
forbidden_side_effects: merging any pull request, including this one, which stops at the merge gate
making any S3 network request to any endpoint, including a connectivity probe, and creating, reading or writing any object
creating, modifying or deleting any bucket, and configuring bucket locks, lifecycle rules or bucket policy through any API
creating, requesting, rotating or inspecting any credential, API token or secret value, and running any command that would echo one
widening the provider enum beyond the two adjudicated classes, and adding a generic any-S3-endpoint escape hatch
permitting a loopback, publicly routable, IPv6, DNS-named or non-canonical endpoint for the self-hosted class
adding a delete verb to the transport, the CLI surface, the contract or the documentation, and emulating create-only with a HEAD-then-PUT
changing the offline CLIs, the live CLIs, the credential loader, the transport, the snapshot format, the manifest, the completeness marker, the verifier or the restore executor
adding a default location, an environment variable, a profile, an instance-metadata path or a provider chain to either live loader
writing a credential value to argv, stdout, stderr, a log, an error message, a report or an evidence file
